correctness.rationale: The unique geometric contact point is rational by Frobenius. Normalize the smooth conic with that point to the Veronese model; restriction of the other quadratic form is a nonzero multiple of s⁴, and the restriction kernel is exactly the defining line of quadratic forms for C. Smoothness makes the coefficient of that defining form nonzero. This gives D=XZ−Y²+λX², λ≠0, with determinant 1/4. Every projectivity preserving C and P induces an affine map w↦aw+b; the restriction to C is faithful (four points on a conic form a projective frame), and the displayed Veronese action realizes these maps. It scales the defining form by a², giving exactly two square classes and stabilizer order 2q. Independently, a finite chord has Z=(u+v)Y−uvX; on X=1 its intersection with D has discriminant (u−v)²+4λ. A chord through P has Y=wX, and restriction of D to it is X[Z+(λ−w²)X], with two distinct intersection points. Thus the graph is edgeless or exactly the coset cycles of h𝔽_p for h²=−4λ, with P isolated. This includes p=3, rationality of the unique tangency on a rational tangent line, and counting modulo the two orientations and rotations. The sign over extension is the n-th power of the original sign, since 1+q+⋯+q^(n−1) has parity n. Orbit–stabilizer gives the claimed sizes and equal census. The frozen verification file and both scripts were inspected, not executed; their finite graphs supplement the all-fields argument.

evidence: The P₈ pencil has one length-four base point and q smooth conics. Table 3.5 gives q(q−1) ordered geometrically 3-Poncelet pairs in that pencil in characteristic 3, zero for other characteristics. Section 2 defines n-Poncelet for finite-field pairs using closure over the algebraic closure.
Wang's cited finite-field transverse eigenvalue criterion and subsequent counts concern other intersection loci.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Classifying pencils up to projectivity and counting all eligible smooth ordered pairs inside a pencil is coarser than computing the orbits of the pairs inside it. The table counts geometric closure and so can count both classes in characteristic three, whereas only one class has rational triangles. Its totals and the single-contact pencil description are prior coverage; the square-class refinement as a projective pair classification is not.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For y≠0, the reciprocal parameters w=1/u and w′=1/v turn the prior H equation into (w−w′)²+a=0. Under the ground-field coordinate change x=Y, y=X, z=Z+aX, their a is the frozen λ. Thus the finite-field tangent splitting is already implicit in the prior formula; evaluating the two-component descent gives the cycles. The arithmetic action on the normal-form coefficients and the ordered-pair stabilizer are different assertions, not stated in those prior passages.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the classification and exact census of ordered rational projective pair-orbits and the identification of their graph/count behavior as an arithmetic orbit invariant. The ground-field normal form, geometric additive porism and incidence discriminant are prior ingredients, and the rational graph count can be extracted from the known incidence equation plus elementary finite-field descent. It is not credited as an independent new tangency equation or porism. The closest finite-field pencil table does not refine the ordered pairs by rational projective orbit. No claim of historical priority is made.
residual_risks: Older projective finite-geometry literature on osculating conic pencils or ordered member-pair stabilizers may contain an equivalent square-class orbit computation.

value.rationale: The invariant of interest is the rational projective type of the ordered pair. A fixed known geometric p-period can arise both from pairs with no rational edge and from pairs with all affine points in rational cycles. Counting the two classes of pairs and identifying that invariant with the graph and its extension behavior gives a useful arithmetic refinement of geometric porism and the finite-field pencil census. Value is not assigned merely for rederiving the geometric period or the known pencil table.
